actual_author_read_scope: All transformed main text, methods, results, discussion, tables as text, figure captions and bibliography read in sequential nontruncated chunks.
not_claimed: No raw PDF or original page/figure raster inspected; transformed numerical units/signs may be faulty.

claims.paraphrase: Main experiments used A. vinelandii206; other named Azotobacter strains remain distinct experimental scopes.
Crude, high-speed and chromatography fractions differed; NADH oxidase interfered with assays.
Catechol cleavage consumed equimolar oxygen. Alternative-substrate oxidation did not distinguish one broad enzyme from multiple oxygenases.
Induced NAD-dependent semialdehyde oxidation dominated; NADase exposed weak noninducible hydrolysis. Endogenous NAD recycling confounded omission controls.
EDTA-trapped product was isolated and compared by melting point and spectra; historical labels do not establish modern intermediate geometry.
Spontaneous spectral conversion and extract acceleration were distinguished; heat stability complicated attribution, while fractionation and induction supported catalysis.
Partially purified preparations coupled decarboxylation/hydration; magnesium or manganese stimulated, EDTA inhibited.
Aldolase fractions produced separately measured acetaldehyde and pyruvate; only42% of synthetic substrate reacted, without absolute stereochemical assignment.
Measured upstream activities increased after benzoate growth; aldolase did not show comparable induction.
The proposed six-step route ends at acetaldehyde/pyruvate. Hydration was not separately characterized; tautomerase physiological necessity remained unresolved.

limits: Historical4-oxalocrotonate explicitly covers enol/keto forms; no exact modernE/Z/S assertion inferred.
